Class NvmlQuery

java.lang.Object
oshi.util.common.gpu.NvmlQuery
@ThreadSafe public final class NvmlQuery extends Object
Backend-independent logic shared by the JNA and FFM bindings to the NVIDIA Management Library (NVML).

Every NVML metric has the same shape: reject a blank device identifier, pair nvmlInit_v2 with nvmlShutdown around the query, acquire a fresh device handle inside that scope, and fall back to a sentinel whenever any step fails. Only the native read differs between the backends, so the skeleton lives here and each backend supplies a one-line reader.

Device handles are valid only within a single init/shutdown scope, which is why the backends exchange stable PCI bus ID strings with their callers and re-acquire a handle for each query.

    • matches

      public static boolean matches(String candidate, String needle)
      Tests whether an NVML identifier matches a sought fragment, in either direction, so that a domain-qualified form matches a bare one: 00000000:01:00.0, 0000:01:00.0 and 01:00.0 all match each other.

      An empty candidate never matches. Bidirectional containment would otherwise make it match everything, because every string contains the empty string, letting a device whose PCI info read back blank answer to any query.

      Parameters:
      candidate - the identifier read from a device, lowercased
      needle - the sought fragment, lowercased
      Returns:
      true if the two identify the same device

    • matchBusId

      public static @Nullable String matchBusId(Set<String> busIds, @Nullable String fragment)
      Returns the enumerated bus ID matching the given fragment, preferring the most qualified form.

      Both of a device's bus ID forms are enumerated, so a bare fragment such as 01:00.0 matches the modern and legacy entries alike. The modern form carries the full eight-digit domain and is therefore the longer of the two, so returning the longest match yields it consistently, and matches what the name lookup returns. Returning the first match instead would let set iteration order decide, which can differ between runs and between the two bindings. A blank fragment matches nothing, rather than matching every enumerated ID as bidirectional containment would otherwise have it do. This is checked here rather than left to matches(String, String), whose guard covers a blank candidate read from a device and not a blank fragment supplied by a caller.

      Parameters:
      busIds - the enumerated PCI bus IDs, already lowercased
      fragment - the fragment to match
      Returns:
      the matching bus ID, or null if none matched or the fragment was blank
